comments.text:
I used a free delivery service from my work cause that’s one of the perks of being an employee, I get to have a Roadie or DoorDash to deliver for free.
I assume my work pays for the services in order to have employees get those for free.

Cause depending on the size of delivery it can be very costly. Small to medium size vehicles is like $15 just to deliver. Medium to huge you are talking about over $25 on top of the amount you paid for the items.

Anyway I used one free service so they could deliver some heavy bags for the garden I have in the back. I can’t carry these bags due to my weight restrictions of 10lbs. I’m not to lift anything above that. I just recently had surgery and can’t move very far without hurting so I need some assistance. I’m not allowed to drive anywhere cause the surgery I had was hip. So for me to get it on my own is out of the question. I need to use the services.

I order the stuff online and use my employee perk so they can deliver my items. Had a gentleman come by and realized my handicap that I have to use a walker or cane. So he offered to take the bags to the back area for storage. 
I know it sucks to not be tipped and grumble when you have an order that says free delivery.

His attitude changed when he saw the predicament I was in. Cause if I could get the items myself I would cause I don’t like to rely on such services when I could get it myself. But this was an exception. I can’t drive till I’m told to and am off for over a month of work.

Well anyway I stopped the man after he dropped the last bag in the back and handed him $10. I didn’t have to but I did cause he used his time and energy to help me out. Basically I payed for the gas cause in my area, it’s like $3.60 a gallon. The delivery wasn’t that far of a drive. I’m like literally 10mins away from a local convenience store. So $10 is fairly reasonable tip.

I don’t do credit card tips. I use actual cash cash. Cause I don’t want to be monitored on my purchases. The government doesn’t need to know all of my business and how much I spend.
If I’ve got the cash I will tip in cash. If I don’t have the cash then I don’t use the services.

This is the only exception cause i can’t drive yet. So I’m shit out of luck and have to use these services till I’m able to drive again.

comments.text: This video is so timely to me having had 2 experiences this week very different: one from d Dasher and one from Instacart. I will add that delivery isn't a luxury for everyone. I'm a senior citizen with a disability that depletes my energy and now I have limited transportation so there are times when I do not have energy to shop. I tip and really do not care if my order gets picked up that day usually and do not want s disgruntled driver shop for me anyway. With Instacart I tip at a low rate and up it if the shopper did a good job. I've tipped 100% before as a holiday bonus. If I tip the expected amount beforehand, there's no telling what condition my food will arrive in honestly. This week the shopper bought the bag of potatoes I ordered. Upon delivery the bag had been switched for an individual potato so I did not receive what I ordered. To me this was a deliberate switch I guess to get more out of the delivery hoping I wouldn't notice or report, but I did both. Then I switched later in the week to DoorDash. I noticed that DoorDash computes tips that include all the fees. I'm not going to pay a tip on fees but I do give a good tip on the actual food. That shopper went over and beyond and very courteous even though it was a small order. Bottom line: If you want to make a living running your own business, attitude is everything. As some have said here, do NOT take it out on the customer. They feed you. Bad reviews will kill your business faster.
